content: Graph memory stores research observations as linked context units.
Stable node identifiers make provenance traces auditable across runs.
Project scope prevents retrieval from crossing workspace boundaries.
Append-only events record changes to stored beliefs.
Token estimates allow context selection to respect a fixed budget.
Supersession preserves historical records while replacing current truth.
Offline compaction removes stale nodes without delaying user queries.
A degree cap limits the number of outgoing graph relationships.
Deterministic ranking makes retrieval results explainable and testable.
Backup and restore rehearsal verifies persistence after a restart.
Graph statistics expose node counts, edge counts, and tag coverage.
A reproducible corpus makes memory-footprint measurements comparable.
